name: screenshots
title: Screenshots
description: Capture an area, a window or the screen to a file or the clipboard, and browse the screenshots you took newest first with thumbnails: open, reveal, copy the image, its path or a markdown tag, read its text, trash it.

settings.label: Every image
settings.text: List every image and recording in the folder
settings.description: Off: only files named like macOS's captures (Screenshot ..., Screen Recording ...).

settings.description: At most this many recent screenshots.

settings.label: OCR copies concealed
settings.text: Text read from a screenshot never enters the clipboard history

store.tagline: Take a screenshot, then find, copy or read the ones you took
features: Capture area, Capture window and Capture screen rows: `screencapture` on macOS (the panel hides first), `grim` with `slurp` on Linux; Enter to a file or the clipboard per the setting, `cmd+enter` after a timer, `cmd+c` to the other destination
The folder's screenshots and recordings newest first, each with a thumbnail, its pixel size, its file size and its age; the HUD names the file a capture landed in
Open, Reveal in Finder, Copy image (the file onto the clipboard), Copy path, Copy as markdown image (`![name](path)`), Copy text (OCR through the Vision framework), Move to Trash
Rows can be marked (`tab`, `x`): open, reveal, copy and trash run over all of them
A screenshot taken in the last two minutes leads the empty root's Now section
The detail pane (`cmd+i`) shows the picture itself with its folder, size, pixels and time

screenshots.caption: Capture area, window or screen, then the folder's screenshots newest first with thumbnails, pixel sizes and ages
Open, reveal, copy the image, its path or a markdown tag, read its text, trash it
The detail pane: the picture itself over its name, folder, size and pixels
